name: Rioja Alta
terms: Denominación de Origen Calificada, a step above DO for regions with a record of consistent quality. Only Rioja and Priorat hold it.
Young wine, sold with little or no aging. Some see a few months in oak.
In Rioja, a red aged at least two years in barrel and bottle, counted from 1 October of the harvest year.
In Rioja, a red aged at least 36 months, with at least 12 in oak. Whites and rosés need 24 months, with 6 in oak.
In Rioja, a red aged at least five years, with at least two in oak and two in bottle.

notes: Oak aging gives Rioja reds pronounced vanilla flavors, long a trademark of the region, though some modern producers use less oak.
Tempranillo has a fairly neutral profile, so in Rioja it is often blended or aged long in oak, where it takes on the barrel's flavor.

Rioja Alta gives wines with body and high acidity suited to barrel aging, Alavesa slightly higher alcohol and a little less acidity, and Oriental, the warmest and driest zone, riper wines suited to blending.
Some white Rioja Reserva and Gran Reserva ages for decades into a highly distinctive, aromatic wine.

blurb.text: One of the three zones of Rioja, a DOCa. Many Rioja wines blend fruit from all three zones, though single-zone wines are slowly growing.
